author: Stone Fox Capital
title: A lot of discussion surrounds whether Apple ( AAPL ) will ra
text:
A lot of discussion surrounds whether Apple ( AAPL ) will ramp up stock buybacks and acquisitions due to the repatriation of foreign earnings provision in the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. A couple of analysts suggest a ramp up in stock buybacks while my previous research doesn't back this theory due to a big repatriation tax hit.
In reality, Apple is likely to make the same moves as the past few years and the market will ultimately reward the stock in part due to the lower risks of having a large war chest full of cash to fight the battles in the competitive technology sector.

Analyst Predictions Both UBS and GBH forecast that Apple will ramp up capital returns and acquisitions due to the tax bill approved by the GOP. The suggestions though doesn't jive with actual of past moves.
UBS analyst Steven Milunovich expects Apple to acquire $122 billion worth of shares through 2019. The amount isn't clear on whether this includes FY19 that sends in September or calendar 2019, but the analyst is likely suggesting $61 billion in annual stock buybacks over two years.
GBH for some reason estimated that Apple would only repatriate $200 billion in cash of the $252 billion in foreign cash and spend that on accelerated stock buybacks and a potentially larger M&A deals. The analyst suggests that Netflix ( NFLX ) is in play though the market cap has already topped $90 billion and would not fit the tradition of smaller acquisition targets by Apple that has helped the company become the most valuable entity in the world.
